edges.description: TBX22 is expressed at the tongue attachment, and its loss leaves an anteriorly placed caudal attachment of the tongue.
Tbx22 is expressed in the nasal mesenchyme where the oro-nasal membrane normally ruptures; in null mice the membrane persists.

edges.limitations: Ankyloglossia is fully penetrant and mild in the mouse, whereas in patients it is partially penetrant and variable.
Choanal atresia was found in the mouse before it was recognised in patients and has since been reported in only a few human families, so its human frequency is unknown.

nodes.description: TBX22 is expressed in the mesenchyme at the base of the tongue in the region of the frenulum in human and mouse embryos. Loss of Tbx22 gives a short, anteriorly attached frenulum, the anatomical basis of ankyloglossia.

evidence.reference_title: Expression of mouse Tbx22 supports its role in palatogenesis and glossogenesis.
evidence.snippet: The localization in the tongue frenulum perfectly correlates with the ankyloglossia phenotype in CPX.

evidence.reference_title: Craniofacial expression of human and murine TBX22 correlates with the cleft palate and ankyloglossia phenotype observed in CPX patients.
evidence.snippet: mRNA is also detected in the base of the tongue in the region of the frenulum that corresponds to the ankyloglossia seen in CPX patients.

nodes.description: Tongue-tie from a short, hypertrophic or anteriorly attached lingual frenulum. Present in most patients and the main diagnostic marker of CPX, but often missed or unreported. It occurs with or without a cleft and is the commonest finding in carrier females.

evidence.reference_title: Unmasking familial CPX by WES and identification of novel clinical signs.
evidence.snippet: In addition to X-linked inheritance, ankyloglossia, present in the majority of CPX patients, is an important diagnostic marker, but it is frequently missed or unreported, as it is a "minor" feature.

evidence.reference_title: The gene responsible for X-linked cleft palate (CPX) in a British Columbia native kindred is localized between PGK1 and DXYS1.
evidence.snippet: Our recent reevaluation of the family has indicated that ankyloglossia (tongue-tie) is also a feature of X-linked cleft palate in some of the affected males and carrier females.

evidence.reference_title: Cleft lip with cleft palate, ankyloglossia, and hypodontia are associated with TBX22 mutations.
evidence.snippet: Mutations R120Q and P389Q were identified in patients with ankyloglossia only

nodes.description: Blockage of the posterior nasal passage, first seen in the Tbx22-null mouse and later reported in human TBX22 families.

evidence.reference_title: Unmasking familial CPX by WES and identification of novel clinical signs.
evidence.snippet: Detailed re-phenotyping of the two probands and their families unravelled orofacial features previously not associated with the CPX phenotypic spectrum: choanal atresia, Pierre-Robin sequence

nodes.description: Complete or partial overt cleft of the secondary (hard and soft) palate, the severe end of the CPX clefting spectrum.

evidence.reference_title: X-linked CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome and classic cleft palate with ankyloglossia result from TBX22 splicing mutations.
evidence.snippet: usually involving either a complete, partial or submucous cleft palate, with or without ankyloglossia

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutation in the X-linked TBX22 promoter disrupts an ETS-1 binding site and leads to cleft palate.
evidence.snippet: we report a loss-of-function mutation in X-linked TBX22 gene (T-box 22) in a six-generation family of the CPO with obvious phenotypes of both cleft palate and hyper-nasal speech

nodes.description: Surgical repair of an overt cleft, and of a submucous cleft when it causes velopharyngeal dysfunction; techniques include palatoplasty, pharyngeal flap and pharyngoplasty. No TBX22-specific surgical data were found; the evidence is from submucous cleft palate of any cause.

evidence.reference_title: Management of submucous cleft palate.
evidence.snippet: Early diagnosis and surgical intervention for SMCP are associated with improved speech outcomes.

evidence.reference_title: Submucous cleft palate: a systematic review of surgical management based on perceptual and instrumental analysis.
evidence.snippet: The review found little evidence to support any specific surgical intervention.

nodes.description: Runx2 expression is initially normal, but alkaline phosphatase activity and the number of differentiated osteoblasts in the posterior palatine osteogenic centre are reduced, indicating a Runx2-independent delay in late osteoblast differentiation.
nodes.id: Delayed Osteoblast Maturation in the Posterior Palate

evidence.reference_title: Tbx22null mice have a submucous cleft palate due to reduced palatal bone formation and also display ankyloglossia and choanal atresia phenotypes.
evidence.snippet: These results therefore indicate a role for TBX22 in Runx2-independent and late differentiation of osteoblasts in the posterior palate.

evidence.reference_title: Craniofacial expression of human and murine TBX22 correlates with the cleft palate and ankyloglossia phenotype observed in CPX patients.
evidence.snippet: We describe TBX22 expression in early human development, where expression is found in the palatal shelves and is highest prior to elevation to a horizontal position above the tongue.

nodes.description: Division of the lingual frenulum for ankyloglossia that impairs feeding. Trial evidence comes from tongue-tie in general, not from CPX, and is limited.

evidence.reference_title: Frenotomy with breastfeeding support versus breastfeeding support alone for infants with tongue-tie and breastfeeding difficulties: the FROSTTIE RCT.
evidence.snippet: Infants were randomly allocated to frenotomy with standard breastfeeding support or standard breastfeeding support without frenotomy.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutation in the X-linked TBX22 promoter disrupts an ETS-1 binding site and leads to cleft palate.
evidence.snippet: a six-generation family of the CPO with obvious phenotypes of both cleft palate and hyper-nasal speech

nodes.description: The oro-nasal membrane normally ruptures to open the choanae. In Tbx22-null mice it persists, narrowing or blocking the posterior nasal passage, with expanded Pax9 expression across the membrane. Choanal atresia has since been reported in human TBX22 families.

evidence.reference_title: Tbx22null mice have a submucous cleft palate due to reduced palatal bone formation and also display ankyloglossia and choanal atresia phenotypes.
evidence.snippet: However, in Tbx22null embryos, a persistent oro-nasal membrane (Fig. 4B), which narrows or blocks this passage, restricts nasal breathing.

nodes.description: Bone formation in the posterior hard palate and the vomer is markedly reduced, leaving the midline notch of the posterior hard palate that defines a submucous cleft. TBX22 acts as a determinant of intramembranous palatal bone formation rather than of palatal shelf closure; overt clefts occur in a minority of null mice.

animal_models.description: The null mouse shows the posterior hard palate notch of a submucous cleft.

evidence.reference_title: Tbx22null mice have a submucous cleft palate due to reduced palatal bone formation and also display ankyloglossia and choanal atresia phenotypes.
evidence.snippet: Rather than having a major role in palatal shelf closure, we show that Tbx22 is an important determinant for intramembranous bone formation in the posterior hard palate, which underpins normal palate development and function.

nodes.description: Occult or overt submucous cleft of the palate, with a notch in the posterior hard palate, often with a bifid or absent uvula. It is one of the most characteristic presentations in CPX families.

evidence.reference_title: A functional haplotype variant in the TBX22 promoter is associated with cleft palate and ankyloglossia.
evidence.snippet: Clinical variability in CPX ranges from a mild or occult submucous cleft palate to a severe, complete cleft of the secondary palate.

evidence.reference_title: The gene responsible for X-linked cleft palate (CPX) in a British Columbia native kindred is localized between PGK1 and DXYS1.
evidence.snippet: A previous clinical description of the clefting defect in this kindred included submucous cleft palate and bifid or absent uvula.

evidence.reference_title: The T-box transcription factor gene TBX22 is mutated in X-linked cleft palate and ankyloglossia.
evidence.snippet: Here we show that CPX is caused by mutations in the gene encoding the recently described T-box transcription factor TBX22 (ref. 14).

evidence.reference_title: X-linked CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome and classic cleft palate with ankyloglossia result from TBX22 splicing mutations.
evidence.snippet: A novel splice donor variant (c.767+5G>A) and a known canonical splice donor mutation (c.767+1G>A) affecting the same exon were identified in patients with classic CPX phenotypes

evidence.reference_title: Novel TBX22 mutations in Chinese nonsyndromic cleft lip/palate families.
evidence.snippet: a novel and essential splicing site mutation, IVS6-1G>C , was detected in a family with cleft palate

nodes.description: Nonsense, frameshift, splice-site, missense and promoter variants abolish or reduce TBX22 function. TBX22 is a sequence-specific transcriptional repressor; pathogenic missense variants cluster in the DNA-binding T-box domain, weaken DNA binding and impair repression, and all of them lose SUMO-1 conjugation at lysine 63, which the repressor activity requires. Promoter variants that lower transcription of an otherwise normal gene produce the same phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: The T-box transcription factor gene TBX22 is mutated in X-linked cleft palate and ankyloglossia.
evidence.snippet: The spectrum of nonsense, splice-site, frameshift and missense mutations we have identified in this study indicates that the cleft phenotype results from a complete loss of TBX22 function.

evidence.reference_title: TBX22 missense mutations found in patients with X-linked cleft palate affect DNA binding, sumoylation, and transcriptional repression.
evidence.snippet: We show that TBX22 functions as a transcriptional repressor and that TBX22 missense mutations result in impaired repression activity.

evidence.reference_title: TBX22 missense mutations found in patients with X-linked cleft palate affect DNA binding, sumoylation, and transcriptional repression.
evidence.snippet: Although the site of SUMO attachment at the lysine at position 63 is upstream of the T-box domain, loss of SUMO-1 modification is consistently found in all pathogenic CPX missense mutations.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutation in the X-linked TBX22 promoter disrupts an ETS-1 binding site and leads to cleft palate.
evidence.snippet: EMSA and ChIP assays demonstrated that the allele A disrupts the binding site of ETS-1, thus markedly decreases the activity of the TBX22 promoter

evidence.reference_title: A functional haplotype variant in the TBX22 promoter is associated with cleft palate and ankyloglossia.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of the patient cohorts stratified for the presence of ankyloglossia significantly increases these associations.

evidence.reference_title: A functional haplotype variant in the TBX22 promoter is associated with cleft palate and ankyloglossia.
evidence.snippet: An important functional role for rs41307258 results in a decreased promoter activity of up to 50%.

evidence.reference_title: Two promoter polymorphisms in TBX22 are associated with the risk of NSCLP in Indian women.
evidence.snippet: Significant associations of rs7055763 (P=0.034) and rs41307258 (P=0.022) with NSCLP were found only in women.

nodes.description: Hemizygous males and homozygous females have a submucous cleft palate, reduced vomer, ankyloglossia in every animal, occasional overt clefts and, in some, choanal atresia that causes about 50% postnatal lethality. Heterozygous females are unaffected.
Inadequate velopharyngeal closure secondary to the submucous or overt cleft, causing hypernasal speech.

evidence.reference_title: Submucous cleft palate: a systematic review of surgical management based on perceptual and instrumental analysis.
evidence.snippet: In a proportion of cases, this results in velopharyngeal insufficiency (VPI), the treatment for which includes pharyngeal flap surgery, pharyngoplasty, and palate reconstruction.

nodes.description: Promoter variant at an ETS-1 binding site, co-segregating with cleft palate without ankyloglossia in a six-generation family.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutation in the X-linked TBX22 promoter disrupts an ETS-1 binding site and leads to cleft palate.
evidence.snippet: The mutation was detected in all five affected male members cosegregating with the affected phenotype and heterozygote occurred only in some unaffected females of the family

nodes.description: T-box domain missense variant segregating with CPX in a Tunisian family with four affected males and two affected females.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation analysis of TBX22 reveals new mutation in Tunisian CPX family.
evidence.snippet: Sequence analysis of TBX22 gene revealed a novel change c.358C>T in exon 3 (R120W) located in the T-BOX domain; this change was present in all affected members and none of the 100 controls.

nodes.description: Canonical splice donor variant found in classic CPX.

evidence.reference_title: X-linked CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome and classic cleft palate with ankyloglossia result from TBX22 splicing mutations.
evidence.snippet: All three variants were predicted to abolish normal mRNA splicing and an in vitro assay indicated that use of alternative splice sites was a likely outcome.
